title: LINGUA Africa -- Gates Foundation / Microsoft / Google.org / Masakhane language-AI grants
description: "Twenty-six projects have been selected under LINGUA Africa, covering more than 50 African languages, dialects and sign languages spoken by over 500 million people across 47 countries -- with each awardee eligible for up to $250,000 in cash and $400,000 in compute credits. The initiative brings together the Microsoft AI for Good Lab, the Gates Foundation, the Masakhane African Languages Hub and Google.org... It follows an open call that closed on 15 June." Healthcare is the largest focus (WHO's AFYA-LINGUA, Makerere University maternal/child health speech dataset, Crails' Luganda medical speech corpus); agriculture (Mohamed bin Zayed University of AI, Kenya's AntuGrow/SemaShambani, AGRA's MlimiVoice Malawi); dialects and sign language (HausaNLP's DialectBridge, Bantu Language Initiative, Arusha Technical College's TSL-Open).

title: Chad - Support Program to Improve the Business Climate and the Modernization of Public Administration (PAACAMA)–Phase I

It will also modernize and interconnect business-development and investment-promotion one-stop shops, establish digital services for special economic zones, improve the legal framework for investment, promote territorial marketing and facilitate the formalization and development of SMEs. The programme comprises three components: (i) support for domestic resource mobilization and stronger external oversight of public finances, (ii) support for improving the business climate, and (iii) programme coordination and management. Activities include upgrading the e-Tax, standardized electronic invoicing and SYDONIA systems; deploying electronic payment terminals and digital platforms; strengthening the National Investment and Exports Agency and the Agency for the Administration of Special Economic Zones; expanding regional business-support services; and supporting incubators, start-ups and young entrepreneurs, particularly in climate-resilient agro-processing, digital technologies and renewable energy. The total programme cost is estimated at UA 10.535 million, equivalent to approximately CFAF 8 billion. It will be financed by an African Development Fund grant of UA 9.52 million, representing 90% of the total cost, and an in-kind Government of Chad contribution of UA 1.015 million, equivalent to about CFAF 724 million. No external co-financing or trust-fund financing is included in the financing plan for this phase. The executing agency is the Ministry of Finance, Budget, Economy, Planning and International Cooperation, through the existing project implementation unit of the Economic Governance and Extractive Sector Support Project. title: ATK Debt II — Atlas Tower Kenya mobile tower expansion
description:
The proposed transaction is a multi-currency senior debt financing of up to US$30 million, including an IFC A Loan of up to US$20 million and remaining to be mobilized from a B Lender/parallel lender for Atlas Tower Kenya (ATK or the Company), an IFC client since 2021. The funding will (i) enable ATK to build and operate new macro towers in Kenya, expanding its existing portfolio of 442 towers; (ii) support ATK's Green Power Program which involves the large-scale deployment of solar power, battery storage, and off-grid or hybrid energy solutions to help reduce dependence on grid electricity and diesel; and (iii) refinance existing indebtedness (Project). ATK is an independent telecommunications infrastructure company operating in Kenya under a build-to-suit (BTS) model. Established in 2018, ATK owns and operates a portfolio of 442 towers and manages the full tower lifecycle, including site identification, land leasing, permitting, construction, energy solutions, and operations and maintenance.

The most significant expected project-level outcome is to increase the capacity of mobile networks in Kenya, resulting in improved access to quality connectivity for individuals and businesses. Beyond the project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will deepen the competitiveness of the mobile tower market in Kenya by expanding shared infrastructure integrating green power solutions via competition channels.

title: Multinational - Strengthening Health Systems and Medical Regulations (SHyMeR) Project

The project will strengthen National Medicines Regulatory Authorities and laboratories, improve access to safe and quality-assured medical and nutrition products, enhance diagnostic and emergency-response capacities, and build the skills of the regional health workforce. It will support the regulatory authorities of Benin, The Gambia, Liberia and Sierra Leone in progressing towards World Health Organization Maturity Level 3; equip The Gambia’s national quality-control laboratory; establish cross-border One Health laboratories in Benin and Togo; and repair, maintain and equip biomedical, diagnostic, intensive-care and cancer-diagnostic facilities in Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia and Sierra Leone. The project will also develop an integrated regional health data hub and electronic medical-record systems, introduce digital learning and virtual or augmented-reality simulation laboratories in three universities, train health professionals and biomedical technicians, and support youth-led biomedical and digital-health enterprises. At the regional level, it will promote harmonized health policies, pooled procurement of essential medicines, sustainable health financing, climate-resilient health investment planning, and the integration of One Health, nutrition and gender-based violence considerations into community-health policies. The total project cost is estimated at UA 11.435 million, equivalent to approximately USD 15.712 million. It will be financed by an African Development Fund Regional Public Goods grant of UA 10.380 million, or about USD 14.262 million, and a cash counterpart contribution from ECOWAS/WAHO of UA 1.055 million, or approximately USD 1.450 million. The grant recipient and executing agency is the West African Health Organization (WAHO). The project development objective is to enhance resilience in West Africa by strengthening health systems and medical regulations to support the provision of quality routine health services and effective responses to public-health and nutrition emergencies in seven eligible ECOWAS member states. title: Morocco – Promoting innovation and the development of the insurtech ecosystem
description: The Moroccan InsurTech, Inclusion and Innovation Programme (PM3I) is a technical assistance operation designed to foster innovation and strengthen the InsurTech ecosystem in Morocco in order to expand insurance inclusion and improve customer experience, particularly for underserved and vulnerable population groups. The total cost of the project amounts to USD 680,000, of which USD 510,000 is financed through a grant from the Africa Digital Financial Inclusion Facility (ADFI) managed by the African Development Bank, while the remaining USD 170,000 is provided as a counterpart contribution by the Supervisory Authority of Insurance and Social Welfare (ACAPS). The project is implemented nationwide in Morocco, with ACAPS acting as the executing agency, and aligns with Morocco’s National Financial Inclusion Strategy and the New Development Model, while benefiting from ADFI’s broader multi-donor platform supported by partners such as the Gates Foundation, AFD, the Government of Luxembourg, the Government of India and We-Fi. The objective of the project is to promote innovation and the development of a robust and inclusive InsurTech ecosystem in Morocco in order to improve access to insurance services and enhance the quality, affordability and relevance of insurance products for vulnerable groups, especially women. The programme seeks to strengthen the regulatory and market monitoring framework, support the emergence of innovative and technology-enabled insurance solutions, and improve the alignment between insurance supply and demand through participatory diagnostics and co-creation of use cases. By reinforcing regulatory capacity, encouraging experimentation and innovation, and supporting change management within the insurance sector, the project aims to create an enabling environment for inclusive insurance, increase trust in insurance services, and contribute to greater financial resilience against economic and climate-related shocks. The beneficiaries of the project include the insurance regulator (ACAPS), 25 insurance companies, around 2,000 intermediaries and brokers, and approximately 30 InsurTech project promoters, whose capacities will be strengthened through regulatory support, training, tools and innovation programmes. The project is expected to directly benefit about 200,000 new insurance users, including at least 100,000 women, as well as 30,000 microenterprises and cooperatives, with a minimum of 40 percent owned or led by women. title: Morocco – Grant project for the establishment of an acquisition fund to facilitate
description: The Africa Digital Financial Inclusion Initiative (ADFI) grant responds to crucial challenges defined by the Central Bank of Morocco at both the national and sector levels. Although Morocco has made significant strides in the development of digital infrastructure and the adoption of technologies, major challenges remain, including the limited use of electronic payments, the heavy reliance on cash, and the weight of the informal economy, representing about a third of GDP. These obstacles hinder the financial inclusion of vulnerable segments of the population, women, young people, and rural populations. Against this backdrop, the project aims at accelerating the transition to digital payments while expanding access to financial services tailored to the needs of all. It helps to bridge the gap between the country's growing technological capabilities, such as high smartphone and Internet penetration, as well as their low use for digital payments. In addition, it plays a key role in mitigating economic risks by reinforcing the integration of marginalized populations into the formal economy, and by developing secure mechanisms such as digital transfers and micro-insurance. Through the African Development Bank, ADFI brings a unique added value through its ability to mobilize dedicated financial resources and coordinate public and private stakeholders. The project seeks to accelerate digital financial inclusion by lowering barriers to entry for merchants, fostering trust in digital payment systems. It combines financial incentives, awareness-raising campaigns, and sound project management practices to create an enabling ecosystem where merchants—particularly women—can adopt and use digital financial services at scale. The project aims at fostering robust and sustainable digital financial inclusion by supporting the development of an electronic payment acceptance network for merchants. The project aims at achieving two specific objectives : (i) developing electronic payments; and (ii) encouraging their adoption to reduce the circulation of cash in Morocco. It seeks to financially include excluded segments of the population, especially recipients of government aid, by creating cases for the use of electronic funds to avoid mass cash withdrawals. At the same time, the project aims at establishing a larger and more profitable electronic payment ecosystem for market players, while democratising these payments through communication and financial education initiatives. The government launched the project through a public-private partnership signed in June 2025 with Trident Digital Tech DRC Africa SAS, a subsidiary of Singapore-based Trident Digital Tech Holdings. The agreement grants the company exclusive rights to provide electronic know-your-customer (e-KYC) services for 20 years." title: TaxDev III
description:
TaxDev aims to contribute to more effective tax and social protection policymaking in low- and middle-income countries through partnerships with governments and researchers. We build new data resources and tools, and conduct skills training, applied policy analysis, and high-quality research.

Taxation is the main source of revenue for governments, and funds vital public services, social protection policies and investments in infrastructure. Tax policy also has significant impacts on individuals and businesses, affecting their incomes, incentives and behaviour. Policymakers need to assess the effects of their tax and transfer systems and use relevant evidence in order to design policies which align with their objectives and foster economic development, poverty reduction and inclusive growth. Rigorous research and analysis are vital.

TaxDev's work has two main components:

1. Country partnerships
We collaborate with tax policy teams in finance ministries and revenue authorities in Ethiopia, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda to co-produce analyses of the key tax and transfer policy and administration issues that they face. The partnerships focus on increasing data resources, building technical skills though applied analysis, and encouraging the use of evidence in the policymaking process. In addition to assessing the revenue effects of polices, we work with partners to undertake analysis of the growth and distributional effects, and crucially to assess how specific policies impact upon low-income households.

As well as informing decisions in particular policy areas, our co-production methodology aims to foster increased analytical capacity within government and support the development of sustainable models, tools and methods which can be used by partners over the long-term.

2. Research
Underpinning our policy-oriented work with partners, TaxDev's research explores the impacts of tax policy and administration on revenue raising capabilities, households, businesses and the economy more widely; and examines how tax policy design responds to changing economic and administrative constraints.

Building on existing research, new empirical and theoretical findings, and insights from the policy work in our partner countries, we aim to generate high-quality evidence which will support governments to design tax systems which raise the revenues required to meet their spending needs, while balancing the trade-offs related to growth, investment and redistribution.

We work with policymakers and researchers across a range of countries in Africa, Asia and South America and pay particular attention to the features of low- and middle-income countries – such as large informal and non-market sectors and more limited administrative capacity - that imply that the impact of, and rationale for, particular policies might differ from high-income countries.

title: Multinational - Designing, mainstreaming and capacity building for gender equity in regulatory frameworks
description: This project concerns designing, mainstreaming, and capacity building for gender-equity in regulatory frameworks. West African Monetary Agency (WAMA)’s project focuses on conducting a gender analysis that will inform the design of gender sensitive policy and regulatory framework reviews. WAMA intends to work with ADFI on mainstreaming gender within the core digital financial services (DFS) regulatory frameworks of the ECOWAS countries/region. To do this, WAMA has singled out the ongoing Regional Payments Framework Gateway as a strategic start to the project that will present an opportunity to execute gender gap analysis in their i) financial inclusion strategy; ii) data analytics strategy for gender disaggregated data; iii) digital payment services such as microloans; iv) digital identity; and v) digital payments infrastructure. WAMA’s business model is to work via the Council of Governors (Heads of Central Banks of the ECOWAS region). Once policy and regulatory revisions are ready, they will be tabled to the Council of Governors, who in turn work with the Council of Ministers. Upon endorsement from Council of Ministers, the revised policies and regulations are shared with Heads of States for review and approval. The expected outputs are: i) detailed implementation plan for the revised policies; ii) gender indicators developed to guide gap analysis; and iii) gender score card developed to track progress. The purpose of the project is to design gender-sensitive DFS regulatory standards in ECOWAS region and the adoption of gender-friendly DFS regulatory frameworks at national and regional levels. The direct beneficiaries are financially excluded women in ECOWAS, the majority of whom are informal traders and an estimated 64% living below poverty line, compared to 68% of the overall population living below poverty line. Indirect beneficiaries are households that rely on women for sustenance, DFS service providers targeting women, government entities across ECOWAS working to address gender disparities in the DFS sector, NGOs and institutions working to improve women’s access to capital, and hence access to DFS services.

title: China Eximbank provides RMB 693 million government concessional loan for Phase II of the National Fibre Backbone Project (Linked to Project ID#52386)
description: In 2018, the Parliament of Malawi passed a Loan Authorization Act allowing the Government of Malawi to borrow $99 million from the China Eximbank loan for Phase II of the National Fibre Backbone Project. In February 2019, Malawi's ICT Minister Henry Mussa held a meeting with China Eximbank officials to reaffirm Malawi's need for more widespread internet connectivity to rural areas. China Eximbank official Zeng Ming promised the project was in the final procedural stages before funding could be released. Then, on August 18, 2020, the Government of Malawi and China Eximbank signed an RMB 693 million governmental concessional loan (GCL) agreement for Phase II of the National Fibre Backbone Project.  The GCL carries the following borrowing terms: a 20 year maturity (final maturity date: March 21, 2040), a 6.5 year grace period (first repayment date: March 21, 2027), a 1% interest rate, a 0.25% commitment fee, and a 0.25% management fee. The proceeds of the loan were on-lent to the Electricity Supply Commission of Malawi.    In a Mid Year Public Debt Report for 2020/2021 Financial Year, Malawi’s Ministry of Finance noted that the loan had ‘registered significant disbursements’. By June 2023, the loan had disbursed RMB 299,286,770.33. The loan's principal amount outstanding was RMB 299,286,770.33 as of June 2023. As of 2022, the borrower expected to make principal repayments each year worth RMB 22,169,390.39 between 2028 and 2040.  The purpose of Phase II is to construct a national data recovery center, lay nearly 3,000 kilometers of fiber optic cables, and install a video-conferencing system in government offices.   Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. is the contractor responsible for project implementation.  Phase II was officially launched by Malawi’s President Lazarus Chakwera on June 29, 2021. description: In March 2015, the Chinese Government and the Government of South Sudan agreed to conduct a feasibility study for the Educational Technical Cooperation Project. The feasibility study was completed in May 2015. Then, on February 3, 2016, the Chinese Government and the Government of South Sudan signed an exchange of letters regarding Phase 1 of the Educational Technical Cooperation Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) reportedly committed $6 million of grant funding for the project’s first phase (captured via Project ID#59201).   Phase 1 involved the design of courses, the training for over 200 South Sudanese teachers in China, the printing of over 1,299,000 textbooks for use by 150,000 teachers and students, and the construction of training centers. China South Publishing and Media Group (中南出版传媒集团股份有限公司) was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Phase 1 officially commenced on June 29, 2016. One month later, on July 29, 2016, MOFCOM awarded a contract to China South Publishing and Media Group. Then, on December 23, 2016, a project implementation agreement was signed by the Chinese Government and the Government of South Sudan. The first phase of teacher training activities was completed in April 2017. During Phase 1, 54 teachers were trained including 14 members of parliament who were members of the education committee. Then, on July 14, 2017, the first batch of 745,000 textbooks and the equipment of the ICT teacher training center arrived in Juba. The second batch of 554,000 textbooks was scheduled for printing by the end of 2017. The project’s first phase passed a mid-term inspection by MOFCOM in December 2017. A one-month ICT training was successfully completed in South Sudan in February 2018. The project’s ICT infrastructure and ICT training component was completed in September 2018. title: China Eximbank provides RMB 560 million government concessional loan for Smart Burkina Faso Project
description: On September 29, 2020, China Eximbank and the Government of Burkina Faso’s Ministry of Security signed an RMB 560 million government concessional loan (GCL) agreement [CHINA EXIMBANK GCL NO (2020) 7 TOTAL NO (699)] for the Smart Burkina Faso Project. The GCL carries a 20-year maturity, a 5-year grace period, and a 1% interest rate. The borrower is expected to used the proceeds of the loan to finance a $80 million (CFA 52,301,810,024) commercial contract (ID# 0Y08541900000) between Burkina Faso's Ministry of Security, Huawei Technologies Co, Ltd and China International Telecommunication Construction Corporation. Huawei Technologies Co, Ltd and China International Telecommunication Construction Corporation are the contractors responsible for project implementation.  The project officially commenced on July 8, 2021 and it is expected to reach completion within 54 months (January 8, 2026).

title: TLCom TIDE Africa Fund I \u2014 LP Commitment (Pan-African Tech VC)
description: BII committed $15M to the TLCom TIDE Africa Fund I in December 2019. TLcom is an Africa-focused venture fund investing in early-stage businesses that leverage technology to solve Africa's biggest challenges. The fund targets fintech, edtech, agritech, and digital health companies across SSA. Portfolio companies include Andela, Okra, Pula (crop insurance), Omnibiz, uLesson (edtech Nigeria), and others. BII is a significant anchor LP.

title: DEG Loan to IPT Powertech for Telecom Tower Energy in Africa
description: DEG provides a long-term loan of USD 25 million to IPT Powertech Group SAL (IPT), a Lebanon-based energy system integrator providing decentralised energy solutions for mobile network operators in Africa and the Middle East. IPT operates more than 30,000 towers in 11 countries in Africa and the Middle East. The loan enables investment in energy solutions to ensure telecom towers remain operational, supporting mobile connectivity across Sub-Saharan Africa including Nigeria, Ghana, and other markets. Co-investors include Proparco (USD 20M), Finnfund (USD 10M), and European Investment Bank (USD 60M).

title: Digital Earth Africa Phase II
description: Phase II of Digital Earth Africa expands the African Regional Data Cube (ARDC) pilot into continent-wide satellite remote sensing data infrastructure for 50+ African countries. Converts 30 years of satellite data into ready-to-use Earth observation products covering flooding, drought, soil and coastal erosion, agriculture, forest cover, land use, water availability and quality, and changes to human settlements. Hosted by UNECA; implemented by Geoscience Australia. Provides free, open data products with no cost to African users.
recipient_organisation: Digital Earth Africa / Geoscience Australia / UNECA

title: DPI investment in Channel VAS mobile fintech platform \u2014 pan-African
description: Development Partners International (DPI), via its African Development Partners II/III fund, invests USD 54 million in Channel VAS (rebranded Optasia in 2022), the leading fintech provider of mobile financial and airtime credit services operating in 30+ African countries, the Middle East, and Asia. Channel VAS provides AI-based mobile financial services, nano loans, airtime credit and big data analytics through partnerships with mobile network operators and financial institutions. Over 85% of revenue derived from Sub-Saharan Africa. Convergence Partners co-invested.

title: Enhancement of Governance and Enabling Environment in the ICT sector (EGEE-ICT) in the East and Southern Africa and Indian Ocean Region
description: Enhancement of Governance and Enabling Environment in the ICT sector (EGEE-ICT) in the East and Southern Africa and Indian Ocean Region - Enhancement of Governance and Enabling Environment in the ICT sector (EGEE-ICT) in the East and Southern Africa and Indian Ocean Region

title: Unlocking Digital Impact for Development (UDID) \u2014 Phase 1
description: FCDO programme implemented by the Digital Impact Alliance (DIAL) to improve digital solutions for development challenges. Supports open-source digital public goods, digital transformation strategies in partner countries, and dissemination of Principles for Digital Development. Africa (including Sub-Saharan Africa) is a primary focus region for DIAL's work on digital public goods, data interoperability, and DPI ecosystem strengthening. The programme promotes standards and governance frameworks for digital development globally, with significant Africa-facing implementation.

title: Digital Identity as an Enabler for Development
description: Supports governments to implement trusted, secure and inclusive digital identification and civil registration systems. Finances the World Bank Group's Identification for Development (ID4D) initiative 2019-2025 to: (1) produce evidence-based guidance on preferred approaches for digital identification and illustrate development value; (2) establish and support global platforms, convening and peer-to-peer exchange; (3) provide technical assistance to over 30 governments and regional institutions to roll out digital identification and civil registration. Also funds independent evaluation of the ID4D programme. ID4D priority countries include Nigeria, Ethiopia, DRC, Kenya and others in SSA.

title: Apis Growth Fund II \u2014 IFC LP Commitment (Fintech/Payments Africa & Asia)
description: IFC committed $25 million as a limited partner in Apis Growth Fund II LP, targeting $400 million in total commitments. Apis Partners invests in mid-market financial services and fintech companies across Africa and South Asia, focusing on payments infrastructure, digital credit, mobile insurance, and distribution platforms. Africa is a primary focus with significant portfolio exposure to SSA fintech and digital financial services. Co-investors include BII, FMO, Proparco, DEG, Swedfund, and EIB.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program \u2014 Digital and Leadership Track (2019 tranche (interpolated))
description: MCF Scholars Program committed $1.7B over first decade (2012-2022) to nearly 40,000 scholars. Target 100,000 scholars by 2030 across 33 partner institutions in Africa. Primarily serves SSA countries. Digital focus includes technology and engineering degrees at CMU-Africa, AIMS, and partner institutions. University of Rwanda 10-year $55M partnership also included.

title: Microsoft Africa Development Centre (ADC) \u2014 $100M Engineering Hub Nairobi and Lagos
description: Microsoft launched the Africa Development Centre (ADC) in May 2019 with initial hubs in Nairobi, Kenya and Lagos, Nigeria — Microsoft's 7th global development centre and first in Africa. Committed $100 million over the first 5 years to recruit 500 full-time engineers building cloud, AI/ML, mixed reality, and Windows products with global impact. By 2022, ADC employed ~570 engineers. Lagos facility expanded March 2022 in Ikoyi. Note: Nigeria ADC closed in 2024 per Bloomberg.

title: Apis Growth Fund II
description: Swedfund invested in Apis Growth Fund II, a continuation of Apis Growth Fund I targeting financial services and fintech companies providing digital financial services to underserved populations across Africa and South Asia. The fund focuses on mobile payment, savings, insurance and credit services. Fund II closed at USD 563 million hard cap in December 2019. Swedfund's prior commitment referenced as part of its ongoing Apis partnership since 2015.
recipient_organisation: Apis Growth Fund II (Apis Partners LLP)

title: UNDP Accelerator Labs Network Africa
description: Network of 33 UNDP Accelerator Labs across Sub-Saharan Africa (Angola, Benin, Burkina Faso, Cabo Verde, Cameroon, Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, DRC, Eritrea, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi, Mali, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Africa, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Togo, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). Each lab focuses on surfacing, testing and scaling locally-sourced innovation solutions to development challenges. Digital prototyping and technology scouting are core activities. Funded by UNDP core, Germany (GIZ/BMZ), Qatar Fund for Development, Italy.

title: Giga \u2014 School Connectivity Initiative for Sub-Saharan Africa (UNICEF-ITU Joint Programme)
description: UNICEF-ITU joint initiative launched in 2019 to connect every school to the internet and every young person to information, opportunity and choice. In SSA, Giga is active in 20+ countries including Kenya, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Niger, Zimbabwe, Benin, Botswana, Namibia, South Africa and Guinea, providing school mapping, connectivity planning, procurement support, and financing facilitation. By November 2023, Giga had mobilized >USD 47.6 million from 14 partners (Ericsson, Dubai Cares, Musk Foundation, SoftBank, BCG, IHS Towers, GSMA, Dell, FCDO, and others). UNICEF is the primary lead of the Giga initiative with ITU as co-lead. Activities include open-source school mapping (Project Connect), real-time connectivity monitoring, government procurement support, and innovative financing models including outcome bonds and connectivity credits. As of 2023, Giga had connected 14,500+ schools globally, benefiting 7.79 million students, with SSA countries (Kenya, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Botswana) accounting for a significant share.
recipient_organisation: Governments of Kenya, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Niger, Zimbabwe, Benin, Botswana, South Africa et al.

title: Digital Economy and Market Development (DEMD) Mechanism
description: USAID Digital Economy and Market Development mechanism supporting digital ecosystem development in Nigeria and Uganda. Covers digital financial services, digital skills, and digital market development.

description: USAID digital services task order covering training, facilitation and digital services across multiple SSA countries including Mozambique, Nigeria, Niger, Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, South Sudan.

title: Young Africa Works in Senegal
description: MCF initial $200M five-year commitment to enable 3 million young Senegalese to access dignified work by 2030. Focus on small businesses, agriculture value chains, education and training. Digital skills and digital economy are core enablers.

title: 9mobile (EMTS) Turnaround Debt Facility
description: AFC approved a USD 230 million senior debt facility (super senior debt investment) to 9mobile (Emerging Markets Telecommunications Services / EMTS, formerly Etisalat Nigeria), Nigeria's fourth-largest mobile network operator. The facility is structured in two tranches: (i) to repay historic vendor obligations, finance costs, and interest reserve account; and (ii) quick-win capex initiatives for network infrastructure upgrade. Purpose is to support 9mobile's turnaround strategy and reposition it for growth and profitability in Nigeria's competitive telecoms market.

title: Establishment of a National Rural Broadband Network (NRBN)
description: Government of India Line of Credit to Nigeria for establishment of a National Rural Broadband Network (NRBN). The LoC was approved by India's Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) on 18 June 2019 and MEA go-ahead granted 25 June 2019. The project aims to extend broadband connectivity to rural and underserved communities across Nigeria through deployment of ICT infrastructure. NRBN implementation is managed by the Federal Ministry of Communications.

title: Partech Africa Series A equity investment in Nomba (Kudi)
description: Partech Africa led a $5M Series A funding round in Kudi (later renamed Nomba), a Nigerian payment service provider enabling digital payments for small businesses and agents. Kudi provides mobile-based financial services and agency banking across Nigeria. Co-investors include Y Combinator CEO Michael Seibel, Khosla Ventures, and Y Combinator.

title: TLcom Capital seed investment in uLesson
description: TLcom Capital led a $3.1M seed round in uLesson, a Nigerian edtech startup founded by serial entrepreneur Sim Shagaya (founder of Konga). uLesson delivers affordable, structured K-12 digital learning content across Africa, targeting learners in Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, Rwanda, Uganda, Sierra Leone, and Liberia via mobile app. This was TLcom's first education sector investment in Africa.

title: Visa Equity Investment in Interswitch Nigeria
description: Visa Inc. acquired a significant minority equity stake (~20%) in Interswitch Group, Nigeria's leading digital payments company, for approximately $200 million. The investment valued Interswitch at $1 billion, making it Nigeria's first fintech unicorn. As part of the strategic partnership, Visa and Interswitch committed to advancing the digital payments ecosystem across Africa.

title: Bank of China provides $41.6 million loan for Phase 2 of the Intelligent Urban Video Surveillance System Expansion Project (Linked to Project ID#58535, #85646)
description: On May 15, 2019, Bank of China and the Government of Cameroon's Ministry of Defense (MINDEF) signed a $41,612,944.52 commercial loan agreement for Phase 2 of the Intelligent Urban Video Surveillance System Expansion Project. According to the Government of Cameroon's Caisse Autonome d'Amortissements (CAA), the loan carries the following borrowing terms: a 2 year grace period, a 11 year maturity, and an interest rate of 6.3%. The proceeds of the loan are to be used by the borrower to finance a commercial contract between the Government of Cameroon’s Délégation Générale à la Sûreté Nationale (DGSN or General Delegation for National Security) and Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., which was signed in February 2017. As of December 31, 2020, the loan had achieved a 76.1% disbursement rate (with an undisbursed balance of CFA 5.3 billion) and its outstanding amount was equivalent to CFA 17 billion.   The project involves the installation of 1,500 video-surveillance cameras in various cities and towns and the acquisition of 2,000 portable two-way radios. During phase 1 of the project, video-surveillance cameras will be installed in the capital cities of the country’s ten regions (Ngaoundere, Yaoundé, Bertoua, Maroua, Douala, Garoua, Bamenda, Bafoussam, Ebolowa, and Buea) as well as the towns of Kribi, Kyé-Ossi. Garoua-Boulaï, Waza, Fotokol, Kousseri and Amchidé.  However, the technical and geographical scope of Phase 2 is unknown. Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. is the contractor responsible for implementation. However, as of February 2022, AidData had not identified any evidence of project implementation.

title: China Eximbank provides RMB 485 million government concessional loan for Phase 3 of NetOne Expansion Project (Linked to Project ID#62426, #62416, #62417)
description: On June 1, 2010, China Eximbank and the Government of Zimbabwe signed an RMB 315 million government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for Phase 1 of the NetOne Expansion Project (captured via Project ID#62416). Zimbabwe’s President Robert Mugabe and Wang Gang, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, witnessed the signing of the loan agreement. The Phase 1 GCL carried the following borrowing terms: a 20 year maturity and a 5 year grace period. However, according to the the 2018 and 2019 Blue Book Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure published by Zimbabwe’s Ministry of Finance and Economic Development, its face value was later revised to RMB 286,080,176.66. The Phase 1 GCL’s amount outstanding (including principal, interest, and arrears) was $42,068,995.10 as of 2021. The Chinese Government also provided an RMB 50 million grant for Phase 1, which is captured via Project ID#62417.    The purpose of Phase 1 was to facilitate the country’s transition to second generation (2G) and third generation (3G) phone technology by expanding the coverage and capacity of NetOne’s network and more than doubling its subscriber base. NetOne Zimbabwe is a company that is wholly owned by the Zimbabwean government. It is one of three mobile phone operators in the country. It used the proceeds of the Phase 1 GCL to purchase equipment from Huawei Technologies and implement network upgrades to wireless broadband stations, while expanding coverage to remote geographic areas lacking service. Its ultimate goal was to reach 7 million subscribers. During Phase 1, a Broadband and Ascot Packet Core Switching Centre in Bulawayo was completed and officially inaugurated on December 7, 2011. By 2012, NetOne had successfully launched mobile broadband and 3G service in Zimbabwe. The geographical areas of the country that received upgraded internet service during Phase 1 included the Southern Region, Matabeleland Province, and Midlands Province. title: CDB provides $70.3 million loan for Video Surveillance Project
description: In 2019, China Development Bank and the Government of Equatorial Guinea signed a $70,325,843.26 loan agreement for a Video Surveillance Project. As such, no principal or interest repayments had been made as of December 31, 2019. No additional details are available, but several Government of Equatorial Guinea sources refer to projects that involved the installation of a video surveillance camera system at the Presidential Palace, the installation of a video surveillance camera system at Malabo International Airport, and the installation of a video surveillance camera system at Malabo-Sipopo Highway. description: Huawei launched its first availability zone (AZ) in South Africa in November 2018/early 2019, becoming the first international cloud service provider with a hyperscale data centre in Africa. Between 2019 and 2022, Huawei Cloud invested more than ZAR 3.5 billion (approximately USD 219 million) in local cloud infrastructure in South Africa, including ultra-large cloud data centres, networks, and services, culminating in the launch of a third AZ in Johannesburg in January 2023. The investment supports IaaS, PaaS and SaaS services for public-sector, financial, telecom, and SME customers across Southern Africa. title: ICBC and Standard Bank provide a ZAR 2.251 billion buyer's credit to Telkom in South Africa
description: In 2019, ICBC (中国工商银行) and Standard Bank (SBSA or 标准银行) have issued a syndicated buyer's credit worth ZAR 2.251 billion to South African telecom giant Telkom. The financing will be funded on a 50:50 basis between both the ICBC and the SBSA. Sinosure provided SA Rand 3.596 billion worth of insurance for this project. The SBSA also provided a down payment facility to facilitate the payment of the 15% deposit. The loan will be used by Telkom for purchasing the new 4G equipment from Huawei which has a value of USD600 million (ZAR9.7 billion) to support its next generation of products, and the loan will have a tenor of 10 years as made possible by Sinosure.. Thie funding is the first ZAR funding raised from China for Telkom.

(2019) 12 TOTAL NO. (495)] for Phase 2 of the Integrated National Security Communications Enhancement Network (ALPHA) Project. The PBC was approved by the Ghana’s Cabinet on October 30, 2019 and Ghana’s Parliament on November 18, 2019. It carries the following borrowing terms: a 20 year maturity, a 5 year grace period, a 2.5% interest rate, a 0% default (penalty) interest rate, a 0.8% management fee ($1,595,309.01), and a 0.5% commitment fee. The proceeds of the PBC are to be used by the borrower to finance 85% of the cost of a  $234,604,266.00 commercial contract between Ghana’s Ministry of National Security, Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., and China Machinery Engineering Corporation (CMEC), which was signed on on December 5, 2018. title: China Eximbank provides RMB 1.225 billion government concessional loan for Konza Data Centre and and Smart City Project
description: In 2017, Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.  and the Government of Kenya’s Ministry of Information, Communication and Technology (ICT) proposed the Konza Data Centre and and Smart City Project as part of a larger Konza Technology City (also called Konza Technopolis) initiative. Konza Technology City was first proposed in in 2008 as part of a Kenya Vision 2030 and began construction in 2013. Then, on April 26, 2019, China Eximbank and the Government of Kenya's Ministry of Finance signed an RMB 1,225,000,000 (Ksh 17 billion) government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the Konza Data Centre and and Smart City Project. The GCL carried the following borrowing terms: a 19.5 year maturity (final maturity date: September 21, 2038), a 7-year grace period (first repayment date: March 31, 2026), a 2% interest rate, and a 0.5% commitment fee. The proceeds of the loan are to be used by the borrower to finance a commercial contract with Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd, which was signed on June 22, 2017.   The lender made disbursements worth RMB 90,653,760.44 between July 1, 2019 and June 30, 2020 (Fiscal Year 2019-2020), RMB 131,870,086.70 between July 1, 2020 and June 30, 2021 (Fiscal Year 2020-2021) and RMB 247,718,790.85 between July 1, 2021 and June 30, 2022 (Fiscal Year 2021-2022).  The loan’s amount outstanding was RMB 90,653,760.44 as of June 30, 2019, RMB 222,523,847.14 as of June 30, 2020, RMB 354,393,933.84 as of June 30, 2021, and RMB 602,112,724.69 as of June 30, 2022.   The purpose of the project is to construct a National Cloud Data Center, Smart ICT Network, Public Safe City and Smart Traffic Solutions, and a Government Cloud and Enterprise Service. The project site is located approximately 61 km from Nairobi, 51 km from Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA), and 400 km from Mombasa. title: China Construction Bank provides $56.9 million loan for Last Mile Connectivity for Rural Area and National Data Centre Project
description: In 2018, the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) agreed to provide a $56,908,596.50 loan to the Government of Malawi for the Last Mile Connectivity for Rural Area and National Data Centre Project. The loan authorization act was passed in the Malawi Parliament on July 26, 2018, and the loan was slated to commence on August 24, 2018. However, in 2019, Malawi’s legislature voted to repeal the loan authorization act that was passed on July 26, 2018, Then, on January 25, 2019, Malawi’s Parliament authorized a $56,908,596.50 loan from China Construction Bank for the same project.   The national data centre entails 136 tower installations to improve ITC (information and communications technology) services for rural parts of the country. The ‘Last Mile Connectivity’ refers to fibre from the National Fibre Backbone Project being connected from landing points to users, facilitated by the towers. The construction of a mobile network tower in Mbvunguti Village, Nankumba in Mokey bay under the project was launched on June 13, 2020. In the current phase, the government is expected to construct 28 towers.

title: Bank of China provides $77.35 million buyer\u2019s credit loan for Phase 1 of National Telecommunications Backbone Project (PBNT)
description: On June 20, 2019, the Shenzhen Branch of Bank of China and the Government of Burkina Faso signed a $77.35 million buyer's credit loan agreement for Phase 1 of the National Telecommunications Backbone Project (PBNT). Then, on October 2, 2019, the Government of Burkina Faso authorized the ratification of the credit agreement. The loan carries the following borrowing terms: a 12-year maturity, a 3-year grace period, an interest rate of 6-month LIBOR plus a 2.5% margin, a management fee of 4%, a commitment fee of 0.8%. The loan is also backed by a Sinosure buyer’s credit insurance policy. The total cost of the buyer's credit insurance premium $6,843,413.73. Bank of China reportedly agreed to provide 60% of the funding needed for the first phase of PBNT while the other 40% would be provided by BNP Paribas. However, on October 8, 2019, the BNP Paribas announced that it was no longer involved in this project. The borrower was expected to use the proceeds of the Bank of China loan to partially finance a commercial contract that it signed with Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.  in July 2014.   The purpose of the project is to construct a 307-kilometer fiber optic network linking the capital Ouagadougou and the city of Po, near the Ghanaian border. This fiber optic ‘backbone’ will have a capacity of 1,600 gigabits per second and will ten municipalities. It is parter of a larger, EUR 175 million program to provide 5,740 km of fiber optic coverage in Burkina Faso, at a cost of 175 million euros. Construction began on December 10, 2017.  Phase 1 was completed and officially inaugurated on October 26, 2021.

title: Chinese Government provides RMB 170 million grant for ICT Modernization Project (Linked to Project ID#92012)
description: On June 26, 2019, the Chinese Ambassador to Chad, Li Jinjin, and Chad’s Minister of Economy and Development Planning, Issa Dubrani, signed a preferential loan framework agreement for the ICT Modernization Project. On the same day, China Eximbank and the Government of Chad signed an RMB 1.316 billion (CFA 111.4 billion or $189 million) government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the ICT Modernization Project (as captured via Project ID#92012). The loan agreement was subsequently approved unanimously by Chad’s Parliament on April 30, 2020. The loan carries the following borrowing terms: a 20 year maturity, a 5 year grace period, and a 2% interest rate. It is secured by (i.e. collateralized against) a minimum cash balance in an escrow account.  The borrower is expected to use the proceeds of the grant and loan to finance a commercial (EPC) contract with Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.   The Chinese Government also issued an RMB 170 million grant in 2019 for the ICT Modernization Project (as captured via Project ID#91949).  The project has three components: the construction of a national data center; the construction of a 1200 km optic fiber cable network spanning the country from south to east (along the Doba-Koumra-Sarh-Kyabé-Am Timan-Abéché-Am Zoer-Guéréda-Iriba axis); and the construction of 50 km loop of fiber optic cables in the vicinity of N’Djamena with 200 2G/3G/4G sites.   Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. is the EPC contractor responsible for implementation. A groundbreaking ceremony took place on July 7, 2020. According to the Government of Chad's Aid Management Platform, the project's originally expected commencement date was May 1, 2020 and its originally expected completion date was October 31, 2021.

title: China Eximbank provides RMB 1.134 billion government concessional loan for Mali Digital 2020 Project
description: On September 28, 2018, the Government of Mali and China Eximbank signed an RMB 1.134 billion (XOF 93,790,872,000) government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the Mali Digital 2020 Project. The borrowing terms of the GCL are unknown. However, it is known that the proceeds of the GCL were to be used by the borrower to finance a commercial contract between the Government of Mali and China International Telecommunications Construction Corporation (CITCC).  The purpose of the project is to lay 817.4 km of intercity fiber optic cable, install twelve OSN 3500 type terminals, install a a GPON (Gigabit Passive Optical Network) urban network with 100 km of fiber optic cable, and install about 50 GPON terminals to interconnect the government institutions. More specifically, the project involves laying fiber optic cables to connecting the cities of Kidal, Gao and Timbuktu to the city of Mopti; laying fiber optic cable along the Gao-Ansongo-Labbezanga-Nigerian border route; laying fiber optic cable along the Kidal-Algerian border route; laying fiber optic cable along the Bamako-Kourémalé-Guinean border route; laying fiber optic cable along the Sevaré – Koro-Burkina Faso border route; establishing a surveillance network made up of 200 cameras and 50 LTE sites; establishing an internal secure communications network for the government; and establishing an electronic identification card system.   CITCC is the contractor responsible for project implementation. In February 2019, Ambassador Zhu Liying visited the construction site and had a discussion with the head of the project team. It is unclear if the project is on track for its 2020 completion date.

title: Multinational - Feasibility study for Gabon-ICT backbone project
description: This intervention concerns the feasibility studies of the Gabon Component of the Central African Fibre Optic Backbone (CAB) project. It includes the setting up of a National Data Centre (Datacenter), a Computer Attack Warning and Response Centre (CSIRT) and a public key infrastructure. These feasibility studies consist of preparing Gabon's interconnection with Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea, and the extension of national fibre optic coverage on the 14 priority axes. This extension goes from the Meyo-Kye-Kyo-Ossi axis (5 km) to the Ndendé-Doussala axis (50 km), via the Lambaréné-Fougamou-Mouila-Ndendé-Tchibanga-Mayumba axis (457 km). In total, a 1,900 km extension, which responds to the main recommendation of the Plan for Infrastructure Development in Africa (Pida), according to which each country on the continent should have at least two fibre optic land links with its immediate neighbours. The project has the following main objectives: (i) to prepare for the interconnection of Gabon with neighbouring countries (Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea) and the extension of national fibre optic coverage; and (ii) to contribute to the establishment of a National Data Centre (Datacenter) in Gabon and a platform comprising a Computer Attack Response and Alert Centre (CSIRT) and a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI). The main beneficiary of the study is the Government of the Republic of Gabon.

title: China Eximbank provides $248.8 million loan for Air Traffic Management System (ATMS) Project
description: On January 25, 2018, the Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan and the South Sudanese Finance Minister signed a preferential loan framework agreement. On the same day, the Government of South Sudan and China Eximbank signed a $248.8 million loan agreement for the Air Traffic Management System (ATMS) Project. The borrowing terms of the loan are unknown. However, it is known the borrower was expected to use the proceeds of the loan to finance a commercial (EPC) contract between South Sudan Civil Aviation Authority and China Harbor Engineering Company (CHEC) Limited, which was signed on October 14, 2016. This loan is reportedly secured by (collateralized against) airport fees/revenues that the borrower is required to deposit in a lender-controlled escrow account.  The loan's amount outstanding was $231,952,567 as of December 2022.  The purpose of the project is to construct Juba ATMS center, a new Air Traffic control tower and operation building, a surveillance system, a navigation system, and a communication system. The Juba ATMS center is located next to Juba International Airport. The project also involves the civil engineering and supporting facilities required by the equipment (such as meteorological facilities), calibration flight test training, and other forms of training for South Sudanese technicians (to prepare them for management of the air space by 2023).   CHEC is the EPC contractor responsible for implementation. Project implementation commenced in June 2020 and it was originally expected to reach completion by June 2023. On July 6, 2021, South Sudan Civil Aviation Authority (SSCAA) announced the launch of a state-of-the-art online system, which allows the opening of new routes. The newly established lower airspace, launched in partnership with aviation solutions provider NavPass, is designed to boost tourism and generate revenue for the economy, according to SSCAA. The CFA 42,754,805,764.67 loan achieved a 98% disbursement rate (CFA 42,077,004,262 out of CFA 42,754,805,764.67). 6 disbursements took place between 2019 and 2020: a CFA 9,568,049,781 disbursement on June 30, 2019, a CFA 15,478,003,812 disbursement on October 31, 2019, a CFA 10,938,194,160 disbursement on January 31, 2020, a CFA 3,896,402,757 disbursement on March 31, 2020, a CFA 827,825,441 disbursement on May 31, 2020, and a CFA 1,368,528,311 disbursement on August 31, 2020. title: China Eximbank provides RMB 567 million government concessional loan for Telecommunications Network Modernization Project (Linked to Project ID#53292)
description: On December 11, 2018, China Eximbank and La Société Comorienne de Télécommunication (Comores Télécom) — a state-owned telecommunication operator in Comoros — signed an RMB 567,000,000 ($85,826,411.40) government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the Telecommunications Network Modernization Project. The GCL carries the following borrowing terms: a 30-year maturity, a 5-year grace period, and a 1% interest rate. The borrower is expected to use the proceeds of the GCL to finance an $81 million commercial contract that it signed with Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. in 2017. More specifically, it involves the extension of a fiber to the home (FTTH) network to 57 additional sites. Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. is the contractor responsible for project implementation. On March 22, 2022, Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. and Comores Télécom officially launched the Nafassi FTTH to provide household access to to high-speed Internet, television and landline telephone services (via submarine cables).

title: China Eximbank provides $73.7 million preferential buyer\u2019s credit for Safe City Project
description: In 2015, Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. submitted an unsolicited bid to the Government of Mauritius to implement a Safe City Project (SCP). Then, on April 1, 2018, China Eximbank and Mauritius Telecom Ltd — a minority state-owned telecommunications company in Mauritius — signed a preferential buyer’s credit (PBC) agreement worth $73,687,000 for the Safe City Project. Police stations in Cote d’Or, St Pierre, La Gaulette, Poudre d’Or, St Pierre and Petit Gabriel in Rodrigues were expected beneficiaries of the equipment and technology. title: China Eximbank provides RMB 438 million government concessional loan for Nation Wide Remote Sensing Airborne Geophysical Survey Project
description: On August 14, 2013, Kenya's Cabinet Secretary for Tourism & Wildlife Najib Balala signed an MOU with Eng Jia Xuetian, President of China's Geological Exploration Technology Institute (GETI) for a nationwide remote sensing, airborne geophysical survey. A commercial contract was then signed on May 19, 2014 for an aerial survey that was expected to result in the creation of a geological map of Kenya's mineral resources (in order to make it easier for investors to make investments in the mineral sector).   On August 31, 2017, China Eximbank and the Government of Kenya's Ministry of Mining signed an RMB 438,000,000 government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the Nation Wide Remote Sensing Airborne Geophysical Survey Project. The loan carries a maturity of 17 years (final maturity date: September 21, 2034). Its other borrowing terms are unknown.   No loan disbursements or principal repayments took place between July 1, 2020 and June 30, 2022 (Fiscal Year 2020-2021 or 2021-2022). The loan’s amount outstanding was zero as of June 30, 2021 and June 30, 2022. title: Ethiopia - Capacity building for financial inclusion in Ethiopia (M-BIRR Mobile Money)
description: The project is anchored with Pillar I of the Bank’s new Financial Sector Development Strategy. This pillar aims at increasing access to financial services to the underserved through technology. The project is also in line with the Bank’s operational focus on financial intermediation and microfinance as well as supporting MSMEs. The project aims to advance financial inclusion and improve the efficiency of the participating five Ethiopian MFIs in Ethiopia with the launch of a shared mobile money platform (M-Birr Mobile Money Service), and the development of an agent network that will expand the reach of the MFIs and formal financial services in general in Ethiopia. It will increase the proportion of poor households and small businesses with access to formal financial services. It will also deepen the financial sector infrastructure and promote the 5MFIs inclusive microfinance model that works for the poor. The total FAPA grant proposed to cover up the launch of the M-Birr Mobile Money Service is for USD 318,000. The project’s objective is to successfully launch M-Birr Mobile Money Service, to be used by the five MFI shareholders, through the newly established AODAO Inclusive Finance Technology Share Company (ShareCo). The ShareCo will be responsible for the operation of the M-Birr platform and brand, and for deploying the training of MFIs staff and agents in the use and provision of M-Birr Mobile Money Service. The launch is to be carried out over a period of (9) months, by initially deploying 1,011 branches and 3,033 agents. With branches and agents, MFIs will be able to reach a larger number of clients farther away from their branches, and offer them efficient and reliable mobile money service. M-Birr Mobile Money service is initially deployed within five regions in Ethiopia, namely, Tigray, Amhara, Addis Ababa, Oromia, and SNNP. Precisely, the project’s beneficiaries will be (i) new clients who, in absence of formal banking services, use more expensive or riskier informal financial services (ii) MFIs who will be enabled to roll out banking services beyond their bricks and mortar network, and (iii) mobile money agents who can develop new revenue streams and create new jobs.

At the time of signing, Zimbabwe was still processing paperwork related to the RMB 33 million transaction from 2015.   This project involved the installation of a supercomputer facility (high-performance computing center) at the University of Zimbabwe. The facility was expected to be used in agriculture, weather forecast, mining, gene technology, and stimulation, and support scientific research in Zimbabwe. The project also involved the training of dozens of Zimbabwean researchers on how to operate the supercomputer.   Inspur Group — China's leading personal computer and server manufacturer — and Dameng were both involved in the implementation of the project.  On February 6, 2015, the project was officially completed and and handed over to the University of Zimbabwe.   In 2017, the Chinese Government supported Phase 2 of this project with an RMB 100 million grant (see Project ID #62405). Another Chinese Government grant was provided in 2018 (see Project ID #62408).

title: China Eximbank provides $98.6 million preferential buyer\u2019s credit for Phase 2 of TelOne Broadband Expansion Project
description: On December 1, 2015, China Eximbank and the Government of Zimbabwe signed a $98,617,482 preferential buyer’s credit (PBC) agreement for Phase 2 of the TelOne Broadband Expansion Project. Then, on April 5, 2016, Zimbabwe’s Parliament ratified the PBC agreement. The PBC carries the following borrowing terms: a 2% interest rate, a 20-year maturity, a 5-year grace period, a 0.25% commitment fee, and a 0.25% management fee. The Government of Zimbabwe, in turn, used the proceeds of the PBC to on-lend to TelOne, a state-owned telecommunications company at a 5% interest rate. The ultimate borrower (TelOne) was expected to use the loan proceeds to finance 85% of the cost of its $116.8 million commercial contract with Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. The remaining 15% was to be directly funded by TelOne. The guarantor of the loan is NetOne (Private) Limited.   The borrower is expected to maintain a minimum cash balance in an escrow account (debt service reserve account) at China Eximbank. In the event that the funds in the escrow account are insufficient to repay the interest and the principal of the loan, the PBC agreement indicates that the extra revenues from an escrow account that was set up for another China Eximbank-financed project (Phase 3 of NetOne Expansion Project, which is captured in Project ID#52620) will be used to settle the TelOne loan.   The borrower is responsible for making 30, equal semiannual repayments between January 21, 2022 and January 21, 2037. The first drawdown (disbursement) took place on March 14, 2017. title: China Eximbank provides RMB 496 million government concessional loan for Phase 1 of National Broadband Network Project (Linked to Project ID#91638)
description: On April 7, 2015, China Eximbank and the Government of Benin signed an RMB 496 million government concessional loan (GCL) agreement [CHINA EXIMBANK GCL NO.35 (2014) TOTAL NO.(538) No. 1420103052015110579] for Phase 1 of National Broadband Network Project. This loan, which is captured via Project ID#58955, carried the following terms: a 20-year maturity, a 7-year grace period, a 2% interest rate, a 0% default (penalty) interest rate, a 0.25% management fee, and a 0.25% commitment fee. The borrower agreed to deposit project-related revenues in a special account to facilitate repayment. The borrower was expected to use the proceeds of the loan to finance a commercial contract between Benin Telecom S.A. and Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., which was signed on August 5, 2014.   The purpose of the project was to expand access to high-speed internet, a fiber optic cable, and 4G technology by rehabilitating a 1060 km fiber optic backbone network that runs from Cotonou to Malanville, constructing a 222 km metropolitan fiber optic loop in Cotonou and surrounding areas, and deploying a 974 km high speed fiber optic broadband network with IMS/MPLS core. The project had six components: 1. Reinforcement of 2000 km of fiber optic cable called the ‘National Backbone’. 2. Building a metro network in Cotonou, comprised of almost 24 km of fiber optic cable. 3. Building a FTTx access network by modernizing sub-distributors of 125 Multi-Service Access Nodes (MSAN). 4. Modernizing a 230 km fiber optic cable line. 5. Creating 30 new 4G base stations. 6. Creating another IP Multimedia Subsystem core network. This project also involved the installation of 48 IP/MPLS routers to extend the IP BTS network. Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. was the contractor responsible for implementation. title: Benin Power Compact \u2014 National Electricity Dispatch Activity (National Distribution Control Center)
description: MCC's $391M Benin Power Compact (signed September 2015, entered force June 2017, closed June 2023) included the National Electricity Dispatch Activity ($31.4M), which financed construction of a national electricity distribution dispatch and control center in Akassato, Abomey-Calavi. The center was inaugurated on 22 June 2023. This is the first national dispatch center in Benin, providing centralised supervisory monitoring and remote control of 41 substations across the national distribution grid. Functions include real-time grid supervision, remote switching, fault detection and dispatch — SCADA-type operational technology. The center connects to the national medium-voltage network to reduce outages, improve reliability, and enable smarter grid management. This was part of the Electricity Distribution Project, alongside the Cotonou Grid Strengthening Activity ($145.3M) and Regional Grid Strengthening Activity ($80.6M).

title: China Eximbank provides $402 million buyer\u2019s credit loan for CEIBA-2 Submarine Cable System Project (Linked to Project ID#484 and ID#58439)
description: In 2006, China Eximbank and the Government of Equatorial Guinea signed a $2 billion oil-backed buyer’s credit facility agreement for various infrastructure projects (captured via Project ID#484). All subsidiary loans approved under this facility agreement carry the following terms: a 5.5% interest rate, a 5 year maturity, and a 2 year grace period. Then, in 2015, China Eximbank and the Government of Equatorial Guinea signed a $402,033,662 subsidiary buyer’s credit loan agreement for the CEIBA-2 Submarine Cable System Project. The proceeds of the loan were used by the borrower to finance a commercial contract between El Gestor de Infraestructuras de Telecomunicaciones de Guinea Ecuatorial (GITGE or ‘Manager of Telecommunications Infrastructure of Equatorial Guinea’) and Huawei Marine Networks Co. Ltd. (Huawei Marine), which was signed in March 2015.   According to the Autonomous Fund for Amortization of Public Debt (Caja Autónoma de Amortización de la Deuda Pública) within Equatorial Guinea’s Ministry of Finance and Budget, the China Eximbank loan for this project had full disbursed as of December 31, 2019 and the borrower had made principal ($87,944,373.00) and interest (6,595,828.00) repayments worth $94,540,201 as of December 31, 2019.   The purpose of the project was to construct the Ceiba-2 Submarine Cable System, which consists of a 400 km submarine cable (with a design capacity of 8 Tbps) connecting Malabo and Bata in Equatorial Guinea, with a branching unit to Kribi in Cameroon.  The Ceiba-2 cable system, which is owned and operated by GITGE, is equipped with an initial 40 Gbps lambda system and is scalable to a 100 Gbps lambda system to meet future demand. The Ceiba-2 Submarine Cable System allows the ACE submarine cable to be interconnected with Cameroon, since the Ceiba-2 and ACE submarine stations in Bata are located next to each other and are interconnected with direct fiber optics. title: ZTE grants $3.5 million USD for the Safe Zanzibar Project
description: In June 2015, ZTE corporation donated $3.5 million USD for the Safe Zanzibar Project which involves installing a CCTV surveillance system in Stone Town. The purpose of this project was to curb crime in Zanzibar, particularly in tourist areas.   According to the reporting from the Habarileo, the entire project was scheduled for completion by the end of 2015. Work plans included the installation of 300 full high definition cameras (FHD) on the main roads of the Stone Town and a command center in Malindi with a video wall and camera control center. The video surveillance system uses Geographic Information System (GIS), case library, and intelligent analysis tools. According to the engineer, with routine management, this system can facilitate sharing information among different administrative departments, utilizing security resources and improving efficiency  of controlling or responding rapidly to major accidents.

title: MTN Ghana (Scancom PLC) 4G 800MHz Spectrum Licence \u2014 NCA Auction
description: MTN Ghana (operating as Scancom PLC) was the sole winner of Ghana's National Communications Authority (NCA) 800MHz spectrum auction in December 2015, acquiring 2x10MHz of 800MHz LTE spectrum for $67.5 million. This was Ghana's first 4G spectrum auction and MTN paid the minimum reserve price, as the three other potential bidders withdrew. The licence enabled MTN Ghana to become Ghana's first 4G operator, launching commercial 4G LTE services in early 2016. MTN deployed additional $18M in site infrastructure for the launch. As of 2021, MTN Ghana had 3.4 million active 4G subscribers and a 82% 4G market share.

title: Egypt - Strengthening the Rule of Law : Enhancing Effective and Transparent Delivery of Justice and Rule-Making
description: The present project is entitled: "Strengthening the Rule of Law : Enhancing Effective and Transparent Delivery of Justice and Rule-Making". It should contribute to consolidating the rule of law and enhancing an enabling business environment. The project aims to design and implement an automated case management system for the Court of Cassation (CC); build capacity of CC staff to use new systems; reduce case delays and improve the provision of judicial services to the public. It should alsopermit a work with the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) to build capacities in legislative drafting and inclusion in the rule-making process comprising activities such as training, technical assistance, peer exchanges, secondments and study tours and IT solutions. The present operation comprises three components, namely: (i) supporting the efficient and effective delivery of justice by the CC; (ii) support transparent and participatory rule making at the MoJ; (iii) project management and monitoring. It should be implemented over a period of 3 years. Overall the project aims at contributing to consolidating the rule of law and enhancing an enabling business environment through (i) enhancing efficiency and effectiveness in the delivery of justice and (ii) strengthening transparency and participation in the rule-making process. The main beneficiaries of the project are: the Government of the Arab Republic of Egypt, the Ministry of Justice, and the populations.

title: China Eximbank provides RMB 623.7 million government concessional loan for the National Backbone Fiber Optic Cable Network and Communication Service Project (AidData Project 58683)
description: On December 14, 2013, the Chinese Ambassador to Niger and Niger's Minister of State for Planning signed a preferential loan framework agreement for the National Backbone Optical Cable Network and Communication Service Project. Then, on January 2, 2014, the Government of Niger and China Eximbank signed an RMB 623.7 million government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the project. The GCL carries the following borrowing terms: a 20 year maturity, a 7 year grace period, a 1% interest rate, and a 0.25% commitment fee. The National Assembly of Niger passed a resolution, ratifying the loan agreement on October 29, 2014. Société Nigérienne des Télécommunications (SONITEL) — Niger's state-run telecommunications operator — is responsible for loan repayment; however, it is not clear if it is the legal counterpart to the China Eximbank GCL or if the Government of Niger used the proceeds of the China Eximbank GCL to on-lend to SONITEL. The project involved the installation of more than 2,275 km of fiber optic cable along three sections (Niamey–Tillabéry, Zinder–Diffa and Agadez–Tahoua), 136 GSM and WCDMA terminals, CDMA and ADSL communication networks, and e-government services. China International Telecommunication Construction Corporation was named as the contractor responsible for implementation, though the source also lists China Communications Construction Co., Ltd. (CCCC) among the "state-owned companies involved" without resolving which company held the implementation contract. Its ultimate objective was to increase national broadband coverage from 54% to 72%. Construction officially began on June 15, 2015 and the project was 95% complete as of November 2016. Construction ended in the first quarter of 2017. The project was officially completed and handed over to the local authorities.
